outcome.ru: Риск реактивации латентных герпесвирусов (ВЭБ, VZV, ЦМВ) в ходе ~6-месячного полёта
outcome.en: Risk of latent herpesvirus reactivation (EBV, VZV, CMV) during a ~6-month mission
outcome.definition: Reactivation of at least one of three viruses (ebv/vzv/cmv_reactivation = 1).

intercept.why: Weakly informative prior (Gelman et al., 2008): the baseline risk is not set in advance.

fitness_index.why: Weakly informative (Gelman et al., 2008): the sign and size of the effect come from the astronaut data. The published effects of Agha 2020 (−29%/−39%) set the weights inside the index and serve as a consistency check, but are not used in the prior because they come from the same study as the dataset (double counting). General-population data (Chastin 2021: HR 0.69) support the direction but do not transfer in size; both variants are in the sensitivity analysis.

sex_male.why: Skeptical: the evidence conflicts. In Stowe et al. (2000) EBV reactivation was more frequent in women (60% vs 35%), in the team's dataset in men. Sex differences in immune responses exist (Klein & Flanagan, 2016), but their direction for in-flight reactivation is not established.

method: Bayesian logistic regression: MAP estimate, Laplace-approximation intervals.

agha2020.citation: Agha NH, Mehta SK, Rooney BV, et al. Exercise as a countermeasure for latent viral reactivation during long duration space flight. FASEB J. 2020;34(2):2869-2881.

chastin2021.citation: Chastin SFM, et al. Effects of regular physical activity on the immune system, vaccination and risk of community-acquired infectious disease in the general population: systematic review and meta-analysis. Sports Med. 2021;51:1673-1686.

gelman2008.citation: Gelman A, Jakulin A, Pittau MG, Su YS. A weakly informative default prior distribution for logistic and other regression models. Ann Appl Stat. 2008;2(4):1360-1383.

klein2016.citation: Klein SL, Flanagan KL. Sex differences in immune responses. Nat Rev Immunol. 2016;16(10):626-638.

stowe2000.citation: Stowe RP, et al. Stress-induced reactivation of Epstein-Barr virus in astronauts. Neuroimmunomodulation. 2000;8(2).

training.source: Agha et al. 2020 (doi 10.1096/fj.201902327R), 22 ISS crew members
